title: Does the epipolar gate survive mismatches that repeat across views?
lede: when a bad feature is wrong by the same offset in more consecutive views, the gate's recall falls from 0.81 to 0.59 at a 10% wrong rate and its lead over a RANSAC start shrinks from 1.7x to a tie within seed noise, though typical errors stay at 2 to 3.5 times the clean floor; a single failed seed in 12 can dominate a mean
summary: sensing-gatemix drew every mismatch independently and flagged that as flattering the gate's voting. Here each bad feature is wrong by the same 10–40 px offset in span consecutive views (1, 2, 4, 8, 12 of a 12-view synthetic rig), at the wrong-match rates SIFT gives after a ratio test of 0.8, 0.7, 0.6 (10.2%, 6.1%, 4.7%, measured by sensing-matchreal). Gate recall falls from 0.81 to 0.59 at 0.8; gate + Cauchy adjustment goes from 0.0031 to 0.0048 object radii (clean floor 0.0014) over spans 1 to 8 while the RANSAC start stays at 0.0051–0.0062, so the gate's 1.7× lead becomes 1.06×, a tie at 12 seeds. One seed in 12 failed outright (0.64 for gate + Cauchy at span 12; 0.24 for plain Cauchy at span 1) and dominates those means. Limits: the span is swept, not measured; synthetic geometry; one image-space offset model, near-miss type only; 12 seeds.
